chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: Recording with Nat Cole: redoing the trio hits note for note
summary: He played on remakes like Mona Lisa and Paper Moon exactly as on the originals and did a few solos; musically the job stifled him.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: She doesn't play anything but the radio. But any way, as you know, that I worked with Nat for quite a few years, and I did quite a few recordings with him. Some of them -- I had some solos. I -- that [was me]. But this was quite a while ago, as a matter of fact this was what Pete Rugolo was doing some writing for him, so you know it's been quite a while ago. We did -- as a matter of fact we have one in particular. I think the first one I did with him You
Stepped Out of A Dream. " And I heard it not too long ago. It wasn't too bad, you know, in retrospect, you know.

But most of the things that I had to do with him -- now, here we come back to identity. See, these things that he recorded previously with a trio he wanted it the same way because they were selling. So he didn't want to change anything. Like Mona Lisa, I had to play it the same way it was done on the record, you know. Okay. And it was Paper Moon, all of these things. The records you hear probably would be with me rather than the original trio, you know, only because they wanted you to redo them. His voice had changed. And it was -- musically I enjoyed -- I admired Nat so much as a musician because -- and as a singer. He was a something else. But for me it was a matter of making money, because musically it was kind of stifling me, you know, it was just -- for me it was just nothing.
